ev.q: Overall, 490 (75%) inquiries concerned persons who had neither traveled to an Ebola-affected country nor had contact with an Ebola patient.
Among these 17, a total of 14 were considered to be PUIs
Of the 61 tested, 35 (57%) had traveled to an Ebola-affected country
Among the 160 persons who had an epidemiologic risk factor, 118 (74%) had at least one sign or symptom
Inquiries averaged 10 per week (range = 1–25) until September 30, 2014
Sixty-one (9%) were tested for Ebola virus, and four were positive, including two travelers.
Among the 650 inquiries described in this report, 107 (16%) occurred after active monitoring was instituted
Symptom history was available for 56 of 57 persons who tested negative for Ebola virus.
During July 9–November 15, CDC responded to clinical inquiries from public health officials and health care providers
after this, the number of weekly clinical inquiries increased, peaking at 227 in mid-October

information on sex and age were available for 82% and 66%, respectively
